name: pdnwebview
tagline: Web Viewer for Paint.NET Project Files
description: Static browser viewer for Paint.NET .pdn projects. The offline pdnexport CLI flattens each file into a full preview, per-layer PNGs, hit-test masks and JSON metadata; the frontend renders those static assets with plain JavaScript, HTML, CSS and WebGL. No uploads and no server-side processing at runtime.
purpose: To make Paint.NET project files viewable on the web without requiring viewers to install Paint.NET.
strengths: Static hosting with no runtime backend or database
Offline pdnexport pipeline for repeatable, cached exports
Vanilla JavaScript/WebGL renderer with layer visibility, zoom and pan
limitations: Requires a separate offline export step before a project can be viewed
Export is CPU- and memory-intensive for large multi-layer files
Layer blend modes are stored but rendered using the Normal blend mode
Limited to Paint.NET files supported by pypdn
installation:
# 1. Viewer + WebGL submodule
git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/chrisb09/pdnwebview.git
cd pdnwebview

# Already cloned without submodules?
git submodule update --init --recursive

# 2. Offline exporter (not needed at runtime)
git clone https://gitlab.com/christianbrinkmann/pdnexport.git ../pdnexport
python3 -m venv ../pdnexport/.venv
../pdnexport/.venv/bin/pip install -r ../pdnexport/requirements.txt

# 3. Local preview with the bundled test project
python3 -m http.server 8000
# open http://localhost:8000/?id=testimage
usage:
# Export a .pdn project (creates data/<name>/)
../pdnexport/.venv/bin/python ../pdnexport/pdnexport.py \
  artwork.pdn data

# Or export every .pdn in a folder
../pdnexport/.venv/bin/python ../pdnexport/pdnexport.py \
  ~/paint-projects data --folder

# Open one or more projects (id = exported folder name)
http://localhost:8000/?id=artwork
http://localhost:8000/?id=artwork&id=logo

# Embed in another page
<iframe src="https://example.com/paint/?id=artwork" \
  style="width:1280px;height:720px;border:0"></iframe>

# Production: copy the viewer and data/ to any static webroot.
# No Python/Node runtime is needed; there is no upload or API.
roadmap: Create a browser extension for quick viewing
Support newer Paint.NET file formats as pypdn adds them
